_comment: Well-known places to look for an ACDC schema, and well-known schema SAIDs named outright.
WHY A REGISTRY IS SAFE HERE, WHICH IS NOT OBVIOUS AND IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. A schema is
content-addressed: its SAID is a digest of the document, so a fetched schema can be
checked against the SAID that was asked for. The registry is therefore a HINT ABOUT WHERE
TO LOOK and not a trust anchor. A hostile or compromised entry cannot substitute a
different schema, because the digest will not match; the worst it can do is fail to
answer, or learn that somebody asked. That is why adding a source is a low-stakes act and
why arcviz may fetch from a source it has no relationship with.
WHAT IT IS FOR. Resolving a schema turns an opaque SAID into a type NAME, and -- more
importantly -- into what the type already IMPLIES. The real Legal Entity vLEI schema
documents its `i` property as 'QVI Issuer AID' and its `a.i` as 'LE Issuer AID', so the
party relation of every credential of that type is stated in the schema. A descriptor that
says 'issued by the QVI to the legal entity' is then restating the type in longer words,
and the algorithm can know that instead of guessing.
THE STATIC MAP COMES FIRST AND NEEDS NO NETWORK. The famous types have stable, published
SAIDs; naming them here answers the common case with no fetch, no latency and no
correlation. Sources are for the long tail.
FETCHING IS NOT FREE AND IS NOT ALWAYS RIGHT. Asking a host for schema X tells that host
somebody is looking at a credential of that type, which is a correlation vector the
dossier specification treats at length. Resolution must therefore be a choice a deployment
makes, not something a renderer does because it can, and the answers are cacheable
forever because a content-addressed document cannot change.

_comment: What arcviz does when a schema cannot be resolved, which is the common case: arcviz's own
corpus contains 38 fixtures and not one schema document, so every SAID in it is opaque.
The four states below must render distinctly. Collapsing the last two is the failure this
repository exists to refuse -- a schema that is merely absent and a schema whose content
does not match its SAID are not the same situation, and only one of them is an attack.

states.means: fetched, and the document digests to the SAID that was asked for
states.render: use the title; treat the entailments as known

states.means: a document was obtained but its SAID was not recomputed, only compared to a self-declared `$id`
states.render: the title MAY be shown and MUST be marked as unverified provenance, per principles.md P12; entailments must NOT be relied on, because an unverified schema could understate what the type implies

states.means: no source answered, or resolution is switched off for privacy
states.render: the schema SAID is an opaque type key: it can say two nodes share a type and cannot say what type. Say so, rather than omitting the type component -- 'unknown type' is true and an absent component is not

states.means: a document was obtained and it does NOT digest to the SAID asked for
states.render: this is a security event, not an absence. Never fall back to it silently, never cache it, and surface it at the gestalt level per posture.md point 6
